steps.step: Every decision needs a group of servers to agree, and a server that does not reply counts as a failure. The cluster keeps working while at least a quorum of servers can reply, so it tolerates (servers − quorum) failures.
steps.part: The setup (the tolerance paragraph and the 5-server and 4-server examples)
steps.idea: The number of failures survived equals the total number of servers minus the size of the group that must reply.

steps.step: Safety comes from overlap. Two groups of sizes a and b can fit inside n servers without sharing a server only if a + b ≤ n. If a + b > n, they must share at least one server.
steps.part: Why the quorum must be a majority (the paragraph on 2q ≤ n vs 2q > n)
steps.idea: The explanation proves this for two groups of the same size q. Counting servers works the same way when the two groups have different sizes; that step is plain arithmetic.

steps.step: For a read to see the latest committed write, every read group must share at least one server with every write group. That shared server holds the write. So W + R > 5, which means W + R ≥ 6.
steps.part: Step 2, plus 'Any two majorities then share at least one server' in Why the quorum must be a majority
steps.idea: The shared server links the two groups. Here the pair is a read group and a write group instead of two decision groups. The explanation only says this server refuses conflicting decisions; that it gives the read the latest value is my inference.

steps.step: Two write groups must also overlap, or split brain could happen between writes: W + W > 5, so W ≥ 3.
steps.part: Why the quorum must be a majority (the split-brain paragraph)
steps.idea: Two separate groups that each make a decision can commit conflicting values.

steps.step: Check W = 4 and R = 2: 4 + 2 = 6 > 5, so reads and writes overlap. 4 + 4 = 8 > 5, so writes overlap with each other.

steps.part: Step 1 (the tolerance paragraph in The setup)
steps.idea: For each operation, failures tolerated = servers − size of the group needed.

result: W and R must satisfy W + R > 5 (that is, W + R ≥ 6) so that every read group overlaps every write group. Writes should also satisfy 2W > 5 so that two writes cannot conflict. With W = 4 and R = 2, both conditions hold. Writes survive 5 − 4 = 1 failure, and reads survive 5 − 2 = 3 failures.
gap: The explanation never talks about separate read and write groups. It proves the overlap rule only for two groups of the same size, so I extended it to W + R > n with arithmetic. It also never says that the shared server lets a read see the latest write; I inferred that from 'any two majorities share at least one server'.
